build: make Prism the default compiler, keep lrama as an option

Swap the canonical gem names so a default build uses the Prism compiler
and tools: the Prism gems take the names mruby-compiler, mruby-eval, and
mruby-bin-{mrbc,mruby,mirb}, while the legacy lrama-based gems are
retained under a -lrama suffix for memory-constrained targets that opt
in. The two compilers conflict, so only one is ever present in a build.

Supporting changes so the full default gembox builds with Prism:
- define global_mrb (the Prism allocator's mrb_state) in the compiler
  library so every executable linking libmruby resolves it, not only the
  mrbc/mruby/mirb front-ends; the tools now declare it extern.
- provide mrb_decode_insn from the Prism compiler (used by mrdb).
- copy node-owned (unescaped) symbol bytes into pool-owned memory in
  nsym so a dumped irep keeps valid symbol names after the AST is freed.
- rename the gem_init/final entry points to match the new gem names.
- bootstrap mrbc with the matching compiler; resolve mrbcfile/installer
  for both name sets.
- full-core excludes -lrama instead of -prism; the CI Prism safety-net
  job becomes an lrama job (build_config/lrama.rb, mrbgems/lrama.gembox).
- point the console build configs at mruby-compiler-lrama.
- update the mrdb syntax-error bintest to the Prism diagnostic format.
